title: Dispatch: 2llo class resource capacities (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Implementation plan for parent eshyra-2llo (read `bd show eshyra-2llo` for defect, scope and acceptance criteria). Supervisor decisions below are made; STOP and record in notes if the code contradicts a premise.

WORKTREE/BRANCH: .worktrees/eshyra-2llo.1 on branch eshyra-2llo.1 (cut from origin/main 18e2e6ce). Deps already installed.

FILE BOUNDARY: a parallel task edits packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts, packages/core/src/rules/featureChoices.ts, packages/core/src/rules/kindSchemas.ts, the importer under packages/core/scripts/importers/, the generated pack under packages/core/data/, and the bonded-summon tools. Do NOT edit those.

CODE SURVEY
- packages/core/src/character/rulesPackResolver.ts parseAdvancement (~line 927): `case 'resourceProgression'` validates `resource` is a string then discards the entry. ResolvedClassLevel (~line 178) has no resource field.
- Pack values (records.json, class progression rows, advancement kind 'resourceProgression'): barbarian `rages` numeric 2..6 and the STRING 'Unlimited' at 20; monk `kiPoints` STRING '—' at 1, then numeric 2..20; sorcerer `sorceryPoints` numeric from level 2 (no entry at level 1). Non-capacity columns: barbarian rageDamage ('+2'..'+4'), monk martialArts ('1d4'..'1d10'), monk unarmoredMovement ('—', '+10 ft.'..), rogue sneakAttack dice.
- packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts (~line 858): the character-ability branch keys counters `ability:${normalizeAbilityName(name)}`, creates them on first spend from a model-DECLARED economy {maxUses, reset} (source 'declared'), and refuses a redeclaration. The combatant branch (~line 790) is the precedent for "economies derive from the record; declared economies fail closed". Table entity_usage_counter: uses_max >= 1, CHECK uses_used <= uses_max, source IN ('record','declared'), reset_kind IN ('recharge_roll','short_rest','short_or_long_rest','long_rest','dawn').
- packages/core/src/character/levelUpEngine.ts: applyLevelUp (~line 437) runs in one transaction: store.save, projectToLiveCharacter, syncSpellSlots, recordProgressionEvent(appliedChanges: changeSet). computeLevelUpChangeSet (~line 603) builds the pure change set.
- packages/core/src/orchestrator/protocol.ts (~line 293-295) tells the model to pass maxUses + reset on a first character-ability spend.
- Feature SRD text for resets: feature:barbarian:rage, feature:monk:ki, feature:sorcerer:font-of-magic.

DECISIONS
1. Classification (record it in docs/design/character-progression.md, new short section): selected expendable capacities = barbarian rages (Rage), monk kiPoints (Ki), sorcerer sorceryPoints (Sorcery Points); gameplay consumer = spend_usage/restore_usage/reset_usage on a character ability. rageDamage = derived damage bonus, martialArts / sneakAttack = dice scaling, unarmoredMovement = speed bonus: all descriptive here (DM-adjudicated via lookup_rules), no deterministic handling. Prose-only capacities (Channel Divinity, Action Surge, Lay on Hands, Wild Shape...) not selected.
2. Resolver retains resources: ResolvedClassLevel gains `resources` (record keyed by the pack resource name) holding the raw value parsed as: number -> {kind:'count', value}; 'Unlimited' -> {kind:'unlimited'}; '—' -> {kind:'none'}; any other string kept as {kind:'text', value} (the descriptive columns). A non-string/non-number value stays malformed.
3. One binding table (usageCounters.ts or a small new module next to it): {classKey, resource, counterKey, displayName, aliases (normalized ability names), reset} for: barbarian rages -> 'ability:rage', 'Rage', aliases ['rage','rages'], long_rest; monk kiPoints -> 'ability:ki', 'Ki', aliases ['ki','ki-points'], short_or_long_rest; sorcerer sorceryPoints -> 'ability:sorcery-points', 'Sorcery Points', aliases ['sorcery-points','font-of-magic'], long_rest. Verify each reset against the feature text and cite it in a comment.
4. spend_usage on a character ability whose stored canonical sheet (createSqliteCharacterSheetStore) has the binding's class and whose normalized ability name is an alias: pack-bound. Any declared {maxUses, reset} is refused (fail closed, message says the capacity derives from the class table). First spend creates the counter from the pack value at the sheet's level, source 'record', canonical counterKey. Value 'none' (monk 1, sorcerer 1 with no entry) -> refuse with a reason (no such resource at this level). Value 'unlimited' (barbarian 20) -> the spend succeeds without consuming or creating a counter; result marks it unlimited. Characters without a stored sheet or of another class keep today's declared behaviour unchanged.
5. Legacy counters: a pre-existing counter under any alias key (e.g. a declared 'ability:ki-points') is adopted on the next pack-bound spend or level-up reconciliation: rekeyed to the canonical key, source 'record', uses_max set to the pack value, uses_used preserved (clamped to the new max). Never two counters for one resource.
6. Level-up: computeLevelUpChangeSet adds `classResources?: [{resource, displayName, from, to}]` (from/to are the resolved values at old/new level; include only bound resources whose value changes). applyLevelUp, inside its transaction after syncSpellSlots, calls one reconcile function in usageCounters.ts that updates EXISTING bound counters only: new uses_max = pack value, uses_used = min(used, new max) (no free restoration); 'unlimited' -> delete the counter. No counter -> nothing (first spend derives it). Ledger gets it through appliedChanges.
7. restore_usage / reset_usage keep their behaviour, operating on the reconciled max. Creature and item counters unchanged.
8. Update protocol.ts's spend_usage guidance in one sentence: class resources (Rage, Ki, Sorcery Points) derive from the class table; never pass maxUses/reset for them. Keep the protocol.test 'no SRD string' rule in mind.

EVIDENCE (real pack; extend existing usageCounters / level-up tests, concise)
- Barbarian 2 spends Rage (counter max 2, used 1); level-up to 3 -> max 3, used 1, remaining 2; ledger appliedChanges.classResources shows rages 2->3.
- Declared maxUses for Rage on a barbarian refused; first spend without declaration creates max from pack.
- Monk 1 Ki spend refused; Monk 2 creates max 2.
- Barbarian 20 Rage spend succeeds unlimited; level-up 19->20 deletes an existing counter.
- Legacy declared 'ki-points' counter adopted and reconciled, single counter afterwards.
- Non-bound character ability (e.g. 'Second Wind' on a fighter) still uses the declared path; existing usageCounters tests green.

PROTOCOL: run `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files); commit on eshyra-2llo.1; append a completion report with `bd update eshyra-2llo.1 --append-notes` (changes, decisions, tests, verify result, follow-ups); file follow-ups with bd create; `bd close eshyra-2llo.1`.
notes: Done, commit on branch eshyra-2llo.1. Resolver retains resourceProgression as ResolvedClassLevel.resources; new state/classResources.ts binding table (rage/ki/sorcery-points with SRD-cited resets); usageCounters.ts pack-binds spend_usage for those abilities (declared economy refused, none refused, unlimited succeeds w/o counter, alias legacy counters adopted) and exports reconcileClassResourceCounters; levelUpEngine adds changeSet.classResources and reconciles inside applyLevelUp txn; protocol.ts sentence; docs/design/character-progression.md classification section; 6 tests in levelUpEngine.test.ts. verify:worktree green (6105 passed, 3 skipped). Decision: spendUsage return type is now SpendUsageResult | SpendUsageUnlimitedResult (unlimited has no counter). Reconcile runs across all campaigns for the character. Uses bundled SRD resolver for spend path (like spellSlots).
